From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — bakeoff scope and timeline

Team —

Draft plan for the bakeoff and save/offering approach (internal):
1) Technical: immediate deliverables for 9/20 start
   - Provision 4x baseline dedicated shard (NVIDIA A10x2) with pre-warmed KV cache and identical model variant to production (gptx-medium-q4).
   - Run three 2-hour steady-state windows that mirror their 08:00/13:00/18:00 peaks; collect latency p95/p99, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization.
   - Provide a per-route tracing hook and token-level cost breakdown CSV for post-analysis.

2) Commercial save play (if we win bakeoff):
   - 12-month committed term (with option to extend to 24 months) on a committed-usage plan.
   - 25% uplift on committed baseline for free for first 3 months of renewal (to cover Q1 seasonal spike).
   - 18% consumption discount on committed token pricing vs list for first year.
   - Dedicated capacity SLA (99.9% uptime) + 2x burst buffer for 14 days post-signing.
   - One-time professional services credit of $15k for migration of their internal adapters and telemetry.

3) Contingency if competitor outperforms on p99 latency:
   - Offer a 30-day performance remediation trial with optimized kernel build and targeted model-quantization tuning; provide SE-led on-site (or virtual) run.

I’ll prepare the technical runbook and the preliminary order form (redwood-final-offer-OF-1834.docx) by EOD. Jordan — recommend we keep Aditya in the thread for any discretionary pricing approvals.

—Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-final-offer-OF-1834.docx)

Jordan / Marissa —

Quick update from the platform team: we ran a small pre-bakeoff with OptimaCloud yesterday (pilot run) and they show a consistent ~20% lower token-cost per inference and slightly better p99 on our long-tail prompts. We’re still doing the formal bakeoff next week, but OptimaCloud has a strong commercial pitch and an engineered runtime for our prompt mix.

Attached is a summary workbook (benchmark-summary.xlsx) with the pilot numbers. Not asking for a reaction yet, but please confirm if the save play you outlined can be tightened — specifically: 1) can Redwood match price-to-win on committed token discount; 2) can you guarantee a p99 remediation window (we need clear SLA remedies); 3) any ability to pilot a 30-day performance-optimized kernel build prior to signing?

If you can get a tightened offer into DocuSign by 9/16 EOD, we can include it in the formal evaluation.

Lina
(Attachment: benchmark-summary.xlsx)
